questions.q: What is the central risk of a data architecture that exists only in the architect's head?
options: Salesforce will not allow undocumented schemas to run in production
It creates a single point of failure — the organization loses the ability to safely change the schema once that architect leaves or forgets the reasoning
Undocumented schemas run slower than documented ones
Governor limits only apply to undocumented objects
questions.explain: The schema itself can usually be read back out of the org, but the reasoning behind each decision cannot — losing the architect without documentation means losing the ability to safely extend or change the architecture later.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's Schema Builder provide, and what does it fall short of providing?
options: It provides a visual diagram of objects, fields, and relationships generated from the live schema, but it does not capture ownership, classification, or the reasoning behind a design decision
It provides a complete architecture decision record automatically
It provides a classification scheme for every object automatically
It replaces the need for a data dictionary entirely
questions.explain: Schema Builder generates a genuinely useful visual relationship diagram directly from the live schema, but it shows structure only — it doesn't capture ownership, classification, or the decision history behind why a relationship was built a particular way.

questions.q: What does an architecture decision record (ADR) capture that a data dictionary cannot?
options: The field-level data type of every custom field
The reasoning and alternatives considered behind a significant decision, not just the resulting fact
The current storage usage of each object
The list of users with access to an object
questions.explain: A data dictionary tells you what a field means; an ADR tells you why a specific decision (like choosing lookup over master-detail) was made, what alternatives were considered, and what would have to change for it to deserve revisiting — judgment, not just a fact.

questions.q: Why can documentation that isn't kept current become worse than no documentation at all?
options: Because stale documentation takes up storage space
Because people trust and act on it even after it has become inaccurate, which is more dangerous than knowing there's no documentation to rely on
Because Salesforce automatically deletes stale documentation
Because documentation cannot be updated once written
questions.explain: Stale documentation is dangerous specifically because people trust it and act on information that's since become wrong — which is why documentation updates should be a required step of the recurring data model review, not an optional afterthought.

questions.q: Which documentation artifact should be written at the time a decision is made, rather than reconstructed from memory later?
options: The data dictionary
The architecture decision record
The Schema Builder diagram
None of these benefit from being written at decision time
questions.explain: An ADR's value comes specifically from capturing the reasoning and alternatives considered at the moment of the decision — reconstructing it from memory months later loses exactly the nuance that made it worth writing down in the first place.
